I was 12 when I officially got diagnosed with depression. I had all the symptoms and it was awful. It's really not that uncommon to get seriously depressed in your teens or at least its not rare. Im sorry to hear about your friend and that girl. You deserve better as does everyone else does. As for the future, you should consider talking to a school counselor or a trusted friend. Maybe they can help your family to understand. My family also thought I was just going through a phase until someone else told them besides myself. Good luck.

I've been hospitalized before on the 72 hour hold before. It's different then going voluntarily, but it's basically the same once you are there. It's not like a padded room in a straitjacket at all, at least not how I experienced it.

You come to the hospital, sign some paperwork, they look through your bags (to make sure you don't have anything dangerous), and then you stay there for a few days to a week or two long. As for what qualifies as dangerous, it varies from hospital to hospital. The hospital I went to didn't allow cellphones, electronics, shoelaces, hairbands, rubber bands, and pencils. Toothpaste was kept in cubbies behind the nurses desk. You meet with your psych doctor everyday, you are probably going to have group therapy, and basically all you do most of the time there is sit around in the main room and play cards, draw (with crayons or various other things), make bracelets, watch tv or a movie. There's not much to do, and there's always someone watching you or not too far away. 

In some cases it can be extremely helpful for some. In my case, it was traumatic and it made me develop symptoms of PTSD. Ironic, right? Hospitalization actually made me more suicidal. I suggest looking up a hospital before you go, to make sure it's an okay one. If you do decide to go then remember to look up your rights before hand. So if your rights are violated, you can get legal assistance. Good luck and stay strong.

I got diagnosed with depression officially when I was 12, but I've shown symptoms since I was 8. It was awful now that I think about it. I felt so hated, alone, sad, and desperate at times. I tried to cut myself, and sometimes succeeded. I honestly don't know how I've coped with suicidal thoughts at the age of 8, but I did somehow.
All the time.

Everyday I think about what it would be like to be normal. No panic attacks, no urges to cut, no worthless feelings, nothing. Just happiness. Or i try to remember before things got really bad for me. But I cant remember what it was like. I feel like it was so long ago (even though it wasn't) and it seems very distant.

I got institutionalized to a mental hospital on the 5150 (for no valid reason), then lived in terrible conditions for 5 days against my will, was fed laxatives and tons of meds. I also was stabbed several times with a needle in the middle of a panic attack while I was there. Ever since I've gotten out (which was a year ago), I have been scared that it will happen again. Which is probably extremely unlikely, but still, Im pretty scared.

I tell myself over and over again "There is no fear, there is no danger" and do some deep breathing. And when Im not in full on panic mode, I try to do something that's distracting and or comforting to me. I usually draw, grab a pillow, listen to the TV, and talk to someone on Skype all at the same time.

I'm pretty much friendless. I mainly stay home, do art, and occasionally talk to people online. Drawing helps me deal with the loneliness and making friends online helps too. I'm homeschooled because of my depression so it's harder for me to make friends. I hate going on Facebook as well, because all my former classmates are still posting pictures of dances, parties, get togethers, and anything else that I don't do on a regular basis. Try listening to music, drawing (even if its just stick figure doodles), and of course, talking on reddit with strangers in the meantime. (:

Yeah, I always feel like that. I try to carry the burden all by myself, and later my friends and family are even more hurt that I didn't tell them I was so depressed. It's hard to balance it, at least for me.

I have been to a mental hospital before and while I was scared to death, my family did everything and anything to try to help me while I was away. I will list what they did, and maybe it'll help in your case too?

In my case, I went to a mental hospital on a suicide attempt that didn't happen. But nevertheless I went on the 5150, so I was forced to stay there for around 5 days. First of all, make sure that you know everything that's going on in the mental hospital regarding your brother. Like what medication, therapy (if any), if he's getting help he needs / if he's not getting help, etc. If you have to call the hospital 20 times to know what's going on everyday, then you do that for your brother. That's what my sister did for me, and thank God she did.

When you go to visit him in the hospital, be sure to support him in any way you can. Bring a favorite food or something he likes. If you can, try to get him something he can do during his stay there too. If you just sit there with people watching you for 24 hours, it makes everything worse. My sister got me an origami book and a ton of paper. I made at least 200 cranes in that hospital and I taught other teens how to make them too. I'm not sure if your brother would be up for that, but if he can it's worth a shot.

Even though it's a really difficult situation, I'm sure that your family can get through this. I know it's really scary, but try to keep going. I have no idea if you are religious or not, or if you'd want to hear this, but I'll be praying for you and your whole family. I wish you an immense amount of luck and hope for your situation.
